task.goal: Produce a governed multi-slide cuisine/food-culture list Carousel in which each list-item slide introduces one distinct dish, anchored by a consistent creator-brand badge, and closes with a comparison slide that clarifies correct versus incorrect phrasing for talking about the dish or the creator's business.
task.success_condition: Every list-item slide shows a visually and nominally distinct dish, the dish-name text overlay stays bound to its matching photo set, the creator's circular brand badge remains uncropped and legible on every slide, and the closing 'Don't Say / Say' comparison slide shows genuinely different copy in each column rather than a repeated placeholder line.
task.atomic_boundary: One curated list of cuisine dishes becomes one ordered carousel slide sequence (cover/list-item slides plus a closing comparison or testimonial slide). No single dish stretched across multiple list slots, no video, no per-slide identity drift on the creator badge.

source_expression_moment.description: The specific dish/list-item narrative moment (e.g. a named regional dish and its serving context) to render on one slide of the sequence.

voice_context.description: The creator's voice, brand badge, and typographic context reference for rendering decisions across the slide set.

carousel_slide_sequence.description: An ordered set of production-ready 1080x1080 slide frames (list items plus a closing comparison/testimonial slide) assembled into one carousel post.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: Food-culture carousels compete against thousands of near-identical recipe-grid posts; the viewer keeps swiping unless each slide reads as one new, nameable dish worth knowing rather than a repeated frame of the same plate wearing a new caption.
stakes: a real regional dish gets flattened into generic 'African food' iconography
the list format collapses into one dish repeated across slots instead of a genuine list
identity_urges: see my own cuisine represented accurately
learn one new dish I can name and try
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer swipes through a bounded list of dishes, each slide anchored to the creator's brand badge, arriving at a comparison slide that clarifies how to talk about the dish or the creator's business correctly.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer names the dish correctly, associates it with the creator's brand badge, and swipes expecting the next slide to introduce a new item rather than repeat the last one.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Remember the name of one dish and the creator who introduced it.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not repeat the same dish's photo set across multiple list-item slides — each list slot must show a visually and nominally distinct dish, or the carousel reads as one dish stretched across several slides instead of a genuine list.

Do not populate the 'Don't Say / Say' comparison slide with identical copy in both columns — the two sides must show genuinely different phrasing, or the slide's entire contrastive function collapses into meaningless repetition.

Do not detach the dish-name text overlay from its matching image grid — the name label must stay visually bound to the specific photo set it identifies, so the viewer never mislabels one regional dish as another.

Do not crop, obscure, or drop the creator's circular brand badge (portrait plus product) from any slide — it is the throughline identity anchor across the whole list; losing it on a single slide breaks source attribution for that item.

Do not present the tweet-style testimonial slide as an authentic, unedited platform capture — the verified badge and handle are a designed template asset, not live-platform evidence, and must not be read as an unmediated real endorsement.
